title: fallback-sequence-runtime-cutover-tf-notes
content:
Purpose:

This is a working-runbook for a fast, observable cutover of the runtime + control-plane for private deployments (VPC/on-prem). It bundles Terraform module upgrade notes, compatibility checks, and a compact rollback sequence. The goal is a safe, reversible cutover for customers who run Redwood Private (control plane + runtime) and depend on pinned API contracts and local caches.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private VPC and on-prem control plane + runtime upgrades where new Control Plane API v2.1 introduces an optional routing header and KV-cache manifest change.
- Customers may be running: terraform-managed infra, k8s runtime clusters (probe-based), KV cache layer (redis or rocksdb), and a self-hosted control plane.
- We assume access to: customer TF state (or guidance to operator), control plane admin kubeconfig, and runtime node SSH when required.

Background / Why this doc:
- Last two upgrades had subtle API header changes that caused customer SDKs to fall back to a slower code path; this playbook focuses on minimizing that exposure and giving operators an explicit fast rollback button.

High-level risk model:
- Low-risk: Config-only changes (flags, feature toggles) can be rolled back quickly.
- Medium-risk: Runtime binary upgrade without DB migration — requires KV warming and validation.
- High-risk: Control plane DB schema changes or state transformation — avoid in the same release window; if unavoidable, prepare offline migration + one-click restore.

Pre-upgrade checklist (must pass before any terraform apply):
- [ ] Confirm customer RBAC and operator contacts; notify 24h/2h/10m before cutover.
- [ ] Capture live metrics baseline (qps, p50/p95, error rates) for 24h. Links: grafana/dashboards/private-<customer>.
- [ ] Snapshot control plane DB and store off-cluster. Command suggestion: pg_dump/pg_basebackup (depends on DB).
- [ ] Export terraform state and stash: terraform state pull > state-YYYYMMDD.json; store in secure bucket.
- [ ] Validate terraform provider versions match module expectations. Run: terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64.
- [ ] Smoke test the current control-plane and runtime health endpoints and list running model workers.

Terraform module upgrade notes (operator guidance):
- Principle: Avoid resource re-creation. If a module renames resources, add a resource alias or run `terraform state mv` prior to applying.
- Example: module/runtime module changed `k8s_deployment.runtime` -> `k8s_deployment.runtime_v2`
  - Plan: terraform state mv module.old.k8s_deployment.runtime module.new.k8s_deployment.runtime_v2
  - If state move not possible, we must plan a canary namespace deploy (see canary step).
- Provider pinning: prefer explicit provider versions in root `required_providers` block. We had one customer with provider v1.2 -> v2.0 drift that changed default lifecycle; pin it.
- Stateful resources: PVCs, secrets, DB endpoints must be left untouched. If module split affects secret names, create shim secrets pointing to same value and update runtime to read both names for a grace period.
- Recommended terraform commands (operator):
  - terraform init -upgrade=false
  - terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan -var-file=customer.tfvars
  - terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json (attach to ticket for review)
  - terraform apply "plan.tfplan"

Rolling upgrade sequence (compact):
1) Preflight (30–60m before cutover):
   - Run a `preflight.sh` that checks: control plane healthy, k8s nodes Ready, redis/rocksdb reachable, model worker counts. Example checks in preflight.sh: curl -sS http://control-plane/health | jq .ok
   - Create a canary namespace: `kubectl create ns runtime-canary-<id>` and apply new runtime image there.

2) Canary validation (15–45m):
   - Route 0.5–1% of traffic to canary (via control-plane routing header or ingress weight).
   - Monitor: latency, token cost delta, error rates, memory and GPU utilization. Required checks must be green for 15m before ramp.
   - Run functional checks: sample generation test vectors, auth flows, streaming/resume tests.

3) Stage rollout (progressive batches):
   - Use batch sizes sized by customer capacity (e.g., 10% increments every 10m).
   - Apply Terraform only to the runtime module that controls canary first. Keep control plane in compatibility mode (see 'compat headers').

4) Final cutover:
   - If terraform changes control-plane resources (ingress, LB), perform during a low-traffic window and keep short TTL DNS or prefer IP failover.
   - After full rollout, flip the optional routing header to default on for 5–10% of requests for 24h before full-enforce (safe ramp).

API compatibility guidance:
- Backwards-compatibility rule: never remove request/response fields without a 2-cycle deprecation. Additive changes only by default.
- Opt-in headers: new routing header `X-RW-Routing: v2` should be ignored by older runtimes. New runtime reads it but will ignore when feature disabled.
- Client fallback strategy: SDK should send both header and legacy X-RW-Legacy=true for grace period; control plane will honour the header if runtime advertises support.
- Compatibility test matrix:
   - control-plane v{a} + runtime v{b} -> expected behaviour. Maintain table offline and attach to release ticket.

KV cache and warmed state migration:
- If the runtime changes the cache manifest format, provide a `--cache-compat` mode that makes the runtime read old manifest and write new. Run warmers to populate caches before redirecting traffic.
- Warm-up technique: run a batch job pulling top N prefixes from production queries and write them into runtime KV. Script skeleton: `python tools/cache_warmer.py --source queries.csv --target runtime-host:9000`

Rollback triggers (stop-and-rollback conditions):
- Error rate spikes > 3x baseline sustained for 10m
- Latency p95 regression > 2x baseline for 10m
- Canary failing functional tests (generation mismatches, auth failures)
- Any state migration failure or irreversible DB error

Rollback procedure (fast path):
- If terraform changed runtime resources only:
  1) Immediately scale new replica count to 0 in k8s for affected namespaces (kubectl scale deploy --replicas=0 ...).
  2) Revert terraform via `terraform apply` using previously saved plan (we stash last plan as plan-prior.tfplan). If plan not available, use `terraform state` + manual state mv back to previous resource names.
  3) For image rollback, set image back to previous tag and `kubectl rollout restart` or `kubectl set image`.
- If control plane DB migration performed (high-risk):
  1) Stop writes (route to read-only or maintenance page).
  2) Restore DB from snapshot (pg_restore or snapshot restore).
  3) Revert control plane deployment via terraform to prior version and redeploy runtime pinned to prior control-plane API.
- Post-rollback: run the same validation suite as preflight and keep the customer informed with timeline and steps taken.

Observability & SLO verification (must be live during cutover):
- Dashboards: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token consumption, model queue length, GPU put/util.
- Tracing: verify end-to-end trace for sample request ID across control plane -> runtime -> model worker.
- Alerting: ensure PagerDuty channel is active and that escalation is configured for the cutover window.

Incident comms template (short, to customer):
- Subject: Maintenance window — Redwood runtime upgrade (ETA window)
- Body: short bullets: what, why, expected impact, rollback plan, contact.

Post-mortem checklist (1–3 days after):
- Collect: terraform plans, applied manifests, logs (control-plane + runtime), snapshots, plan.json.
- Measure: token-cost delta, latency delta, error delta.
- Decide: whether to keep compatibility shim or schedule follow-up patch.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] We need a one-line API compatibility header spec that SDKs can follow. Draft in tracker RDW-1577.
- [ ] Build a helper: `tf-state-mapper` to make rename-safe upgrades across our module splits.
- [ ] Add an automated cache warmer job template to the TF module for customers who opt-in.

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Extract TF state: `terraform state pull > /tmp/state-$(date +%F).json`
- Move resource in state: `terraform state mv 'module.old.module["runtime"].kubernetes_deployment.runtime' 'module.new.module["runtime"].kubernetes_deployment.runtime_v2'`
- Canary deploy: `kubectl apply -f k8s/runtime-canary.yaml -n runtime-canary-<id>`
- Quick healthcheck: `curl -H 'X-Request-Id: cutover-123' http://control-plane.local/healthz`

If anything in this runbook is unclear or you hit a blocker, ping #eng-private-deployments and add RDW ticket to the linked_artifacts list.

-- end --
